hints.title: Read necessary in the right direction
hints.body: To show a condition is necessary, every function with equal left and right integrals must satisfy it. A condition that merely guarantees the equality is sufficient.
hints.pitfall: Even symmetry is a sufficient route to equal areas; that does not prove it necessary.
hints.pause: Try to satisfy the integral equality without one listed condition.

recall.reminder: Necessity and sufficiency are opposite implications and need separate tests.

hints.title: Test a simple even function
hints.body: Try <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math>. Calculate the two integrals and then test whether this function is constant or odd.
hints.recap: A counterexample to necessity satisfies the target but fails the alleged requirement.
hints.pitfall: Being even does not by itself answer whether the other properties hold.
hints.pause: Decide what your computations establish about conditions II and III.

recall.reminder: A counterexample to necessity satisfies the target but fails the alleged requirement.

hints.title: Test equality without matching heights
hints.body: Try <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>25</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>. Integrate over each half-interval and compare <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.
hints.recap: Integral equality concerns totals, while evenness concerns paired individual values.
hints.pitfall: A proposed functional counterexample must pass the integral test as well as the pointwise test.
hints.pause: Complete both calculations and decide whether condition I is necessary.

recall.reminder: Integral equality concerns totals, while evenness concerns paired individual values.

solution:
For necessity, we need the integral equality to force each stated property.

Take f(x)=x2. Both integrals equal 1253, but f is neither constant nor odd. Thus II and III are not necessary.

For I, take g(x)=x3−(252)x. Its integral over [0,5] is [x44−25x24]05=0. As g is odd, its integral over [−5,0] is also 0. Yet g(1)=−232 and g(−1)=232, so g is not even.

Therefore none of I, II or III is necessary: A. I and II are sufficient, which is a different claim.
knowledgePattern: Disprove necessity of symmetry conditions for equal integrals
